title: Heartbead Bracelet
category: Bracelet (beaded strand with a front toggle clasp and 1 hanging heart charm; two tone; supplier SKU YF5215)
metal: Two tone. Strand: rhodium silver tone, mirror-polished surgical stainless steel spheres (tag 'Rhodium Plated'; listing 'polished silver tone steel'). Clasp and heart: 18k gold tone (listing: 'PVD 18K gold coated clasp and charm, anti-tarnish'), high polish. The only gold parts are the T-bar, the toggle ring, the jump rings and the heart; every bead and the 2 end links are rhodium silver tone.
lock: 1 bracelet, 18 cm: 25 round 6 mm mirror-polished rhodium silver tone steel spheres on 1 continuous strand with thin flat collars between them; at each end 1 small 3 mm silver bead and 1 silver link. 18k gold tone clasp at the front: 1 straight plain T-bar, 1 smooth round toggle ring, and 1 puffed polished heart (about 15 mm) on 1 jump ring from the ring's base. The 25 spheres must stay rhodium silver tone mirror steel, never pearls or gold beads.
morph: The strand. Image models read 25 grey mirror spheres as pearls and repaint them with soft pearl lustre, or warm them toward gold. Both have happened. The live listing's own photo 04 (hf_20260912 png, sage felt) is a Higgsfield frame that drifted to pearlescent grey pearls; its alt text even says 'each grey pearl'. Night Shift flagged it, and it is still on the listing. In The Red Room, frame R09 mixed gold beads into the strand. Second risk is the gold hardware. Models swap the toggle for a lobster clasp, move the heart onto the bar or let it hang from the strand, add a second heart, or flatten the puffed heart into an open outline, a locket or an engraved disc. They also tend to insert chain or link runs between beads (the listing copy invites this; see copyNotes). Third risk: dark gunmetal or hematite-black beads, which listing photo 05 leans toward.
sizeMm: Listed: 18 cm long, fits wrists about 15.5 to 16.5 cm ('length is approximate'; size guide photo 07, the same file the description embeds as 08). Beads about 6 mm and heart about 15 mm (description). Measured from photo 01, these proportions are estimates: the heart is about 1.8 bead widths across (about 11 mm wide if the beads are 6 mm, so the listed 15 mm reads as its drop including the bail), the toggle ring outer is about 1.6 bead widths (about 10 mm), the T-bar about 2.7 bead widths (about 16 mm), and the 2 end beads about half a bead (about 3 mm). The count of 25 beads plus the clasp fits the listed 18 cm only at about 6 mm per bead, so 6 mm holds. An earlier generated-plate check measured 7.4 to 7.6 mm, inside its 30% tolerance. Body referent: worn (photo 05) on a slim wrist just above the wrist bone, the toggle and heart sit on top, about 7 beads cross the visible back of the wrist, and the heart is about the size of a fingernail. The colour-camps check measured the heart at about 13.6 to 17 mm against a 58 mm wrist and 10 mm fingernails.

claims: Waterproof, Tarnish Free, Hypoallergenic (all three are tags; the care text also says 'Waterproof and tarnish free, so daily wear and water are fine'). The listing also says anti-tarnish PVD and surgical stainless steel. Nothing else: no 'sweatproof', 'lifetime', 'never fades' or 'nickel free'.
variants: 1 variant: Default Title, two tone (rhodium silver tone strand with an 18k gold tone clasp and heart), stock 11. That is down from 29 in Sept/Oct, so it is the fastest mover among the earlier hero SKUs. Price ₹999. Earlier ads ran ₹1,299 and spent ₹1,540 on story 'S1', so old price copy must not be reused. There is no metal choice, so always show it two tone. Photos (concept-50/refs/heartbead-bracelet/): 01 = clasp macro on a cream plaster cube. It shows the bar-side end bead with its silver eye pin and link, the gold T-bar and ring, the gold jump rings, and the heart's bail. It is the same unit as 06 (mid cool-grey mirror beads, flat-ended bar). This is ref 2. 02 = 640 px supplier shot of the bracelet wrapped on a burgundy linen roll. It is the only current photo where the beads read bright mirror silver, which is what the copy describes, but it is low resolution. Use it as a tone check only. 03 = blush Naira gift box, no jewellery. 04 = Higgsfield sage-felt frame: DRIFTED, beads became grey pearls. Never use it, and ask the owner to pull or replace it. 05 = worn on a wrist, cream wall. True scale, but the beads read dark gunmetal and the T-bar has ball tips, unlike the flat ends in 01, 02 and 06. Use it for scale only and do not pass it as a reference. 06 = whole bracelet draped on a plaster cube: all 25 beads, both small end beads, the bar, the ring and the heart. This is the construction authority and ref 1. 07 and 08 = the same size guide (18 cm, fits 15.5 to 16.5 cm). Use them to measure only; their text would leak. Show the clasp at the front with the heart hanging free below the ring. The strand reads cool steel and the heart is the only warm thing in frame.
story: One small warm note on a cool wrist. 25 tiny convex mirrors, each holding a reflection of the room, then a single puffed 18k gold tone heart where the toggle closes. It is the one piece in the catalogue that never had to choose a metal (Night Shift 'Two Metals': 'The Heartbead never had to choose'). It rhymes with ball bearings, mercury beads, a string of disco-ball spheres, an abacus row, conversation hearts (Sugarplay S3 'SWEETHEART.' stamped listing facts on candy hearts), and a cloakroom ticket (Red Room R3 'CLOAKROOM.': 'Redeem for one Heartbead bracelet'). It also fits a steel watch with one gold thing (the listing's own styling tip), and gifting yourself (Night Shift 'The Gift': 'From: you'). It suits the Keep It On shower frame too, where it passed and the waterproof tag backs it. What sold and what didn't: on pale grounds it lost (VK S1 on pastels spent ₹1,540 with 0 sales, and 'One warm note.' on a fabric roll spent ₹141 with 0 sales). The rule from that test is that dark, saturated grounds (oxblood, cocoa, red velvet, deep sage) win. There, the mirror spheres pick up the colour and the gold heart pops. Crazy directions with that in mind: a chrome-ball pinball or Newton's cradle with 1 gold heart in the row; 25 spheres reflecting 25 tiny faces or rooms; the heart as the 1 warm pixel in a cold steel kitchen; a mercury thermometer where the heart is the reading; a magnet or ball-bearing hardware-store 'parts list' with the price as the part number.
copyNotes: Use: 'Heartbead Bracelet', 'mirror-polished steel spheres', 'rhodium silver tone strand', '18k gold tone toggle and heart', 'PVD 18K gold coated', 'two tone', 'surgical stainless steel', 'puffed heart', 'toggle', '6 mm', '18 cm, fits wrists 15.5 to 16.5 cm', 'one warm note', 'waterproof', 'tarnish free', 'hypoallergenic', '₹999' / 'Rs 999'. Avoid: 'pearl', 'pearls' or 'grey pearl' (it is steel; the listing's own photo 04 alt text is wrong), 'hematite', 'gunmetal' or 'black beads', bare 'silver' or 'gold' (say 'rhodium silver tone' and '18k gold tone'), 'sterling', '925', 'solid gold', 'locket' (the heart does not open), 'hearts' (there is exactly 1), 'lobster clasp', 'chain bracelet' or 'link bracelet'. Also avoid the listing's 'short runs joined by fine silver links': every photo shows 1 continuous strand with links only at the 2 clasp ends, and repeating that line invites a model to add chain sections. Do not use ₹1,299 or ₹1,540, which are old ad prices and spend figures. No brand comparisons.
